doc.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Becoming a Buddhist through Robin Eubanks and Wayne Shorter
summary: Eubanks and Shorter led her to Soka Gakkai Buddhism; she explains the Gohonzon, Nichiren and the Lotus Sutra.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Was your interest in Buddhism, did it have anything to do with music or meeting people through music?

Yes. Robin Eubanks always talked to me about Buddhism but when I met Wayne Shorter he really got me into the practice. He lived in California and Robin lived in New York and I was living in New York at the time. So once I really developed the interest I went back to Robin and, you know, tell me more. And he took me when I received Gohonzon which is a scroll that is used as like an object of worship.

G-O-H-O-N-Z-O-N. And it’s called — well now it’s changed its name to Soka Gakkai International. And it’s basically a Buddhist philosophy that’s based on a man named Nichiren Daishonin and he was around about 700 years ago, and it’s based on Sutra, that Shakyamuni Buddha, the original Buddha, he wrote many teachings and many writings over the years but — my stomach, you hear that? — but the Sutra that he wrote that this Buddhism is based on is the Lotus Sutra. And the Lotus Flower that grows out of mud and it’s this beautiful thing that comes out of mud. And he only wrote one more Sutra after that, the Nirvana Sutra. So the thing is you have hundreds of kinds of Buddhisms because there were so many different writings and people will focus on maybe one area of what he had to say. But this was towards the end of his life and he said disregard my previous teachings. This is kind of what I’ve arrived at. So that’s why, because some of the things that happened before are maybe things I didn’t necessarily connect with or agree with. But when somebody says okay I’ve really learned and I’ve grown and this is what I have to say about life, and that’s the one I connected with, to me it’s obvious then to maybe disregard some of the earlier ones, which some people that focus on the earlier ones, and plus he traveled through India and China and Japan and Buddhism traveled through all these countries in the East and over the course of his life he did a lot of traveling so you have all these different people that picked up on what he had to teach at certain times in his life. So now you have like hundreds of Buddhisms. So anyway this particular one is Nichiren Daishonin. His influence, how he was received Soka Gakkai teachings and then he was kind of a Buddha of the later day.
There’s not too many Buddhists three thousand years ago. So we’re dealing with a lot of time. It’s obviously older than Christ.
